part_title: AWS and Customer Responsibilities for AI Workloads

scenes.title: AWS Shared Responsibility Model
scenes.narration: Look at the diagram's two sides. On the left, AWS secures the infrastructure of the cloud: physical facilities, underlying hardware, managed service foundations and infrastructure availability. On the right, the customer protects what they configure and use: identities, permissions, business data, applications, encryption choices, logging and service-specific security settings. The stacked blocks in the middle show that the exact boundary depends on the service. Follow the Bedrock example across the bottom. Your users authenticate, your application handles requests, Bedrock operates the managed model-serving infrastructure, and your organization still controls what information it sends, who may call the service and how outputs are handled. A fully managed AI service reduces your infrastructure work; it does not transfer ownership of your private data or acceptable-use decisions to AWS. For an exam question, first identify the AWS service, then ask which layer AWS operates and which controls remain yours.

scenes.title: Shared Responsibility: AI Workload Example
scenes.narration: This slide applies the same principle to a Bedrock question-answering assistant. Read the five customer responsibilities on the left: prompts and context, IAM policies, retrieval data sources, guardrail configuration, and application-level monitoring. Those arrows point to the central managed Bedrock service because your application decides what it sends to the model and what it permits the model to access. On the right, AWS operates service infrastructure, foundation-model hosting and scaling, the service's underlying security, and platform maintenance. The lower flow shows a user asking a question, an authorized application retrieving material from a source such as S3, a Bedrock response using configured safeguards, and the business reviewing outputs. The exam distinction is practical: AWS runs the managed model service, but your company must restrict the retrieval source, protect user data and investigate harmful or inaccurate answers.
